Research suggests these controls for the fixed HSTU benchmark: baseline, +text, +normalized sampled softmax, +hard-negative curriculum, then targeted combinations/removals. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, splits, candidate sets, capacity, negative count and training updates matched; cap training at 200 epochs × 200 batches and log all GPU time against 43,200 seconds. Separate cosine normalization, temperature and sampling-distribution correction; compare uniform, immediate-hard and warmup-to-hard sampling at matched mining cost. Sampled softmax already emphasizes difficult negatives, so curriculum gains may overlap with temperature effects ([Wu et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02327)).

For text, proposed shortcut controls: capacity-matched ID-only inputs, length/missingness-only features, fixed-length truncation, and text shuffled between items within training-popularity/length bins. Train these controls independently; inference-time removal alone measures distribution shift. Report gains by training-popularity, text-length and history-length strata; inspect score/embedding-norm correlations with popularity. Track centered item and final-history embedding spectra, variance and cosine similarities; effective rank = exp(−Σpᵢlog pᵢ), with pᵢ normalized singular values ([Roy–Vetterli](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.40328)). Higher rank alone does not establish better recommendation. Monitor negative-score quantiles, gradient concentration and hard-negative overlap with observed training positives.

Prespecify comparisons and checkpoint rules; report every attempted configuration. Repeated validation selection creates optimism ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). For uncertainty, resample paired user hit differences within each category, then average four category means; report 95% intervals and discordant-user counts. These intervals condition on seed/candidates and do not remove selection bias. With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves macro HR@10 by 0.125 percentage points. Keep the 99-negative evaluator unchanged; sampled-ranking gains need not imply full-catalog gains ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Use validation only; no test labels or predictor fusion.
